title: Robotic Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Comprehensive Narrative Review of Techniques, Outcomes, and Future Directions
content:
Robotic coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) has evolved over the past 25 years from an experimental technique into a mature surgical strategy practiced at specialized centers worldwide. Two principal approaches—robotic-assisted minimally invasive direct coronary artery bypass (RA-MIDCAB) and totally endoscopic coronary artery bypass (TECAB)—offer patients complete avoidance of median sternotomy, with reductions in blood transfusion, wound complications, length of stay, and pain. Hybrid coronary revascularization (HCR), combining robotic left internal thoracic artery (LITA) grafting with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for non-left anterior descending (LAD) vessels, extends the reach of robotic surgery to multivessel and left main disease.
Robotic CABG represents a safe, reproducible, and durable alternative to sternotomy CABG for selected patients with single- and multivessel coronary artery disease. Broader adoption remains constrained by steep learning curves, cost considerations, and limited surgical training Randomized controlled trials comparing robotic CABG with conventional CABG and PCI are needed to define the optimal role of this technology in contemporary revascularization practice.
